newsitem.title: UK: British trade deficit slashed as exports soar.
newsitem.headline: British trade deficit slashed as exports soar.

text.p: Britain's trade deficit with the rest of the world narrowed sharply in October as exports soared, official figures showed on Tuesday.
Britain's trade deficit was pared to 454 million pounds ($760.1 million) in October from 1,059 million the month before, the Office for National Statistics said.
But more up-to-date figures on Britain's trading position with non-European Union nations showed a trade deficit of 639 million pounds in November, well above October's 418 million shortfall.
Government ministers welcomed the figures. Treasury minister Phillip Oppenheim said they showed exports were on a strong upward path.
Britain exported goods worth 14.62 billion pounds to the rest of the world in October. In September, total exports fell just short of 14 billion.
"These figures again show that growth is broadly balanced and illustrate the growing success of the British economy," Oppenheim said. ($1=.5973 Pound)
